Dear [Mrs.

Craik](../persons.html#378),
Your note and enclosure have followed me to the home where I am staying a few days (in spite of the address on my paper).

Many thanks for it.
I read with much interest the account of the [Little Sisters](../others.html#197) in the Magazine.[^1] It is curious how they make their way with all kinds of people, even at Plymouth, the last place where I should have expected them to thrive.[^2]

Yours sincerely

C M Yonge

[^1]: \'Good Catholics, being the history of \"Les Petites Soeurs des Pauvres\"\' by Henriette de Witt appeared in the January 1868 issue of [Macmillan\'s Magazine](../others.html#78).

[^2]: No doubt because of Plymouth\'s strong Nonconformist tradition and the opposition which had met Lydia Sellon’s attempts to establish a sisterhood there.
